about: Every parameter of the reference-datacenter model (reference_dc.py), each with its unit and source. Hardware values are datasheet values until compute-research's (Phi dense FP8, memory, sigma, the inventory's shape) replace them: swap them here, nowhere else. 'spec' is Daniel's spec of 25 Oct 10:05 PM PDT as relayed by the training lead; 'tiers' is benchmarks/nci/tiers.py's DEFAULTS. Every parameter with a 'range' is in the tornado; the range's source says where its ends come from.

requests_per_year.source: spec: about worldwide inference by Sept 2027 (Epoch)
requests_per_year.range_source: guess: a quarter to four times the spec

decode_tokens.source: spec: a parameter, prefill only by default as top's sanity numbers

b_tok.source: spec: 17-bit tokens (README: raw token ids carry about 17.3 bits)

session_output_bits.source: spec: a session returns at most 2.5 MB (1M tokens at 20 bits)

n_active.source: spec: DeepSeek-V4-Pro, 49B active, served in FP8

kappa_F.source: spec: training work = 6 x active params x tokens, so 6 FLOP per counted forward product

batch_tokens.source: spec: one optimizer step, a 94.4M-token batch

state_bytes_per_param.source: spec: training state about 1.6e12 params x 16 B with Adam (fit.py B_TRAIN adam, 128 bits)

h100_flops.source: NVIDIA H100 SXM datasheet: FP8 dense 1,979 TFLOPS (3,958 sparse); spec: 1 H100-hour about 7.1e18 FLOP at 100% use

sigma.source: spec: real accelerator speed against the FLOP model; 1 until compute-research sends it
sigma.range_source: guess: MFU-like 30% to the datasheet peak

window_s.source: spec: a server-window is the 24 h between wipes
window_s.range_source: guess: hourly wipes to the spec's daily

k_inference.source: spec: the policy point k = 2e7 bits (calibrations.json kimi-k2-1m-raw K)

phi_F_mode.source: spec: 'model' is 2 x 49e9 / 17 FLOP per novel bit (this model's 17-bit tokens); 'traffic' is the traffic calibration phi_F_traffic

phi_F_traffic.source: spec: the traffic calibration for DeepSeek

R_device_bytes.source: spec: Daniel, the wipe residual is at most 5 GB per device
R_device_bytes.range_source: guess: a tenth to ten times Daniel's 5 GB

R_scope.source: spec: a switch, 'device' (R_device_bytes per GPU) or 'location' (R_device_bytes per server or rack)

I_cert_multiplier.source: spec: certified ingress per server-day is the server's share of the committed requests' input tokens at b_tok; this scales it

beta_side.source: spec: side channels 1 kb/s per server (per location), swept 1e-1 to 1e7

r_hat.source: tiers.audited_residual: capacity outside the compute certificate (uncredited GPU time, host CPUs, the clock above credit). 0 here: the fleet is sized to the committed work at full use, so the certificate covers all of it, and the spec's U is PoUW's deficit, certificate slack and escapes only. The fleets' host_share_peak says what host CPUs would add
r_hat.range_source: 0 to the H200 server's host CPUs at INT8 AMX peak (host_share_peak, about 3%) plus margin

eps_w.range_source: exposure.RANGES eps_w: best plausible design 0.06% (C7 dossier); CircuitCredit 0.681-0.917% over r = 1-4

p_window_fail.source: tiers eps_agg: per-window certificate failure 3 x 2^-40; certificate slack eps' = p_window_fail / delta by Markov's inequality over the windows

lag_s.source: tiers: verdict lag, a window plus the verdict delay, from a first faulty proof block to the halt: all declared work skippable once per identity

identities.source: tiers: identities a detection doesn't end (detection terminal, J = 1)

sampled_share.source: tiers share: sampled proofs' compute share

sampled_overhead.source: tiers overhead: proving cost per unit of step work (sparse draws today)

sampled_step_bits.source: tiers step_bits: output bits per sampled step a failing block can choose (a proof unit's outputs are at most 16 bits)

sampled_floor_steps.source: tiers floor_steps: steps in a class drawn at a floor of one

escape_share.source: escaped faulty blocks as a share of the period's compute; null derives it from sampled proofs (luck x identities x ln(1/delta) / q blocks of sampled_step_flop, q = share / (overhead + replay), tiers.evaluate's skipped work). A number overrides it
escape_share.range_source: guess: none to a tenth of a percent

deltas.source: spec: delta = 1% and 1e-6 wherever probabilistic terms enter

horizons.source: spec: monitoring periods; a month is a twelfth of a Julian year

fan_beta_x.source: spec: joint activation premise, cheapest boundary (d = 7168, FP8); note:training-20261024T2336Z-report-tvi-findings ties it to the exact-block measurement (0.87-0.94 at FP8 on Qwen2.5-1.5B)
fan_beta_x.range_source: the cheap-input block's 0.030 at FP8 (layer 0) to the per-layer reading 2.7 (withdrawn, note:training-20261024T2336Z-report-tvi-findings)

fan_beta_x_per_layer.source: spec: the per-layer reading, each layer's products at its own boundary's rate

fan_x_lead.source: spec: token-reachable leading-layer products excluded from T-fan's count, 0.3-0.8% at the inference block (FP8); the upper end, the adversary's side

fan_b_upd.source: extrapolation (ours): at a block of K bits, the token-reachable share is at least the share of parameters whose update at b_upd fits in K (leading layers' share of products taken equal to their share of parameters); 2.5 is C1's floor b_w, the adversary's side (8 at FP8)

thread_e.source: spec: Lambda = max(e, c_reuse k / (4 d b_w)) with DeepSeek's e

thread_d.source: tiers d: 1 is what Lean certifies for a run that trains its embedding (ReferenceThreaded's 10 for Kimi K2 is under the open conjecture ReferenceLayered)
thread_d.range_source: tiers d; ReferenceThreaded's d under its conjecture

thread_c_reuse.source: Nci.Threading reuse: 2 in a standard transformer (forward and backward to the activations); tiers.lam fixes it at 2, so a counted multiplication is half a forward product's training work

cover_b.source: UpdateHardness's b (CoverTraining; Kimi K2's 2.5 in CoverFanOut.lean)

cover_unit_products.source: flagged normalization (ours): CheckedCoverTraining counts products at the declaration's gate granularity, a Dot16 step, so a counted unit may be worth 16 scalar products; 1 reads it as one scalar product. The honest conversion is open
cover_unit_products.range_source: one scalar product to a Dot16 step's 16

exfil_sync_bits.source: spec: at least 17 GB a sync

exfil_weights_bits.source: spec: the weights, 0.8 TB at FP4

exfil_rollout_bits.source: spec: 100M tokens of R1-style RL rollouts, about 21 MB at 17 bits a token with about 10x compression

coop_syncs.source: spec: the cooperating dark share's run takes 1,000 SparseLoCo syncs of exfil_sync_bits each, every one crossing side channels

h200-server.about: eight-GPU H200 servers (DGX H200); a location is one server

flops.source: 8 x H200 SXM FP8 dense 1,979 TFLOPS (DGX H200 datasheet: 32 PF FP8 sparse); datasheet until compute-research's Phi

hbm_bytes.source: DGX H200 datasheet: 1,128 GB total GPU memory (spec: about 1.1 TB)

host_bytes.source: DGX H200 datasheet: 2 TB system memory

nvme_bytes.source: DGX H200 datasheet: 8 x 3.84 TB NVMe U.2

host_Bps.source: 8 x PCIe Gen5 x16, 64 GB/s each way per GPU

nvme_Bps.source: estimate (ours): eight Gen4 U.2 drives at about 6-7 GB/s reads

nic_bps.source: DGX H200 datasheet: 8 x ConnectX-7 at 400 Gb/s (compute fabric)

host_share_peak.source: estimate (ours): two Xeon 8480Cs, 112 cores x 2,048 INT8 AMX ops per cycle x 2.0 GHz base, over the GPUs' FP8 dense rate (tiers' host_share method)

nvl72.about: GB200 NVL72 racks only; a rack is one location with NVLink inside

flops.source: GB200 NVL72 spec page: FP8 720 PFLOPS sparse, 360 dense (spec: 360 PF); datasheet until compute-research's Phi

hbm_bytes.source: GB200 NVL72 spec page: 13.4 TB HBM3E (spec: about 13.8 TB, 72 x 192 GB)

host_bytes.source: GB200 NVL72 spec page: 17 TB LPDDR5X

nvme_bytes.source: not counted: the host memory holds the overflow

host_Bps.source: GB200 NVL72 spec page: LPDDR5X 14 TB/s (NVLink-C2C 900 GB/s bidirectional per superchip, 36 of them)

nic_bps.source: estimate (ours): one 400 Gb/s ConnectX-7 per GPU

host_share_peak.source: estimate (ours): 36 Grace CPUs, 72 Neoverse V2 cores at about 256 INT8 ops per cycle and 3.1 GHz, over the GPUs' FP8 dense rate
